clue.text: Ineffectual type, king going into decline

indicators.note: one thing going into another ends up sitting inside it

parts.note: a dip is a fall or decline
R, from Latin rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A weak monarch whose reign is sliding downhill.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes inside DIP to make DRIP.
explanation.definitionFit: A drip is informal slang for a feeble, wet, spineless person.

clue.text: Cheese and bun deli has prepared

indicators.note: food that has been prepared has been worked over and made into something new

explanation.surface: A delicatessen has made up some cheese and a bun, a snack order.
explanation.definitionFit: Danish Blue is a well-known blue-veined cheese made in Denmark.

clue.text: One approaches overwhelming defeat, finally weeping

indicators.note: to overwhelm is to engulf, so one word wraps round the other
finally points to the closing letter of the word it follows

explanation.surface: A competitor on the brink of a crushing loss finally breaks down crying.
explanation.walkthrough: I, then NEARS wrapped round T: I + NE(T)ARS.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in tears is crying, the same state as weeping.

clue.text: Mixed tapes, lucid copies

indicators.note: mixed suggests the letters are jumbled together in a new order

explanation.surface: A sound engineer's mixed tapes yield clear copies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mixed tapes' reads as a music term, but mixed is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Duplicates are exact copies of an original, and both words work as noun or verb.

clue.text: Less than regular parts of track we tackle

parts.note: under means less than, as in under ten

indicators.note: regular parts are taken at even intervals, every other letter

parts.note: first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: Athletes taking on a track only in short regular stretches.
explanation.definitionFit: To undertake a job is to take it on, which is what tackling a task means.

clue.text: Shrub that's shown up in botanical illustration

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top
in says the letters sit inside the following words

explanation.surface: A flowering bush pictured in a botanical drawing.
explanation.definitionFit: Lilac is a shrub of the genus Syringa with fragrant purple or white blossoms.

clue.text: Kindly captain initially just accepting team on merit

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so one word holds the others
on means placed directly after, so one piece follows the other
initially points to the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: to rate is to merit, deserve

explanation.surface: A fair-minded captain picks the team purely on merit.
explanation.walkthrough: C, then ONLY holding SIDE + RATE: C + ON(SIDERATE)LY.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindly as an adverb means acting with thought for others, which is what considerately describes.

clue.text: Judge occupied by competition to make ornamental stonework

indicators.note: a word occupied by another has that other living inside it

parts.note: to try a case is to judge it

explanation.surface: A judge busy with a contest for carved masonry.
explanation.walkthrough: Try is what a judge does to a case in court, so the judge here is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Tracery is the decorative interlacing stone ribs in Gothic windows, an ornamental form of masonry.

clue.text: Democrat supporting witness in beginning

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means placed underneath, so this piece comes after

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for Democrat

explanation.surface: A party member backs a witness at the start of a trial.
explanation.definitionFit: A seed is the origin or germ of something, as in the seed of an idea.

clue.text: Observed number bound to catch cold

parts.note: No. is the abbreviation for number

indicators.note: to catch something is to trap it inside, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: C stands for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone noticed that a numbered person was certain to catch a chill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' looks like a leap or a certainty; here it means tied up.
explanation.definitionFit: Noticed and observed are plain past-tense synonyms for having seen or registered something.

clue.text: Vehicle expert upset during escapade on a large rocket launch site

indicators.note: something happening during an event sits inside it
on means added next, so the following pieces come after

parts.note: a caper is a lark or escapade
L is the clothing abbreviation for large

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so read from the bottom

explanation.surface: A driving expert gets upset during a big adventure involving a rocket.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed vehicle-and-expert pair is pushed inside the escapade after its third letter, with A and L tacked on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Cape Canaveral in Florida is where NASA and others launch spacecraft and rockets.

clue.text: Time, attached to rope, to make descent

indicators.note: attached to means joined on behind, so the first piece follows the second

parts.note: a line is a rope or cord
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A climber clips a rope on and takes time to abseil down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Descent' looks like a climber going down; here it means ancestry.
explanation.definitionFit: Lineage is line of descent from ancestors, one's ancestry or pedigree.

clue.text: Distinct cost about pretence and chicanery

parts.note: sharp as in a distinct, clear image

indicators.note: about means going around, so one word encircles the next

parts.note: the price is what something costs
putting on an act is a pretence

explanation.surface: A clear charge for trickery and deceit.
explanation.walkthrough: SHARP + PR(ACT)ICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharp practice is dishonest but barely legal dealing, which is what chicanery means: trickery.

clue.text: Referring to church with quiet story about candle's first holder

indicators.note: about means going around, so one word encircles the other
with means alongside, so the pieces are simply joined

parts.note: re means concerning or referring to
CE is the Church of England
p, piano, is the musical mark for quiet

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A quiet tale told in church about a candle and what holds it.
explanation.walkthrough: RE + CE + P + TA(C)LE.
explanation.definitionFit: A receptacle is any container or vessel that holds something, a general holder.

clue.text: Major airline? So essential

parts.note: BA is British Airways, Britain's flag carrier
sic is Latin for so, thus

explanation.surface: Is a big airline therefore indispensable?
explanation.walkthrough: Sic, Latin for 'thus', is used in quotations to mark a slip as original.
explanation.definitionFit: Basic and essential both describe what is fundamental or necessary at the core.

clue.text: Model car involved with publicity surrounding Spielberg film

indicators.note: with means alongside, so the pieces are joined in order
involved means tangled or complicated, so the letters are jumbled
surrounding means going all round, so one word encloses the other

explanation.surface: A model car is part of the hype around a Spielberg blockbuster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model car' reads as a toy, but Model is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An archetype is the original model or perfect example from which others are copied.

clue.text: Certain deception very popular with December coming up

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for very

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means read from the bottom upward

explanation.surface: A particular trick proves a big hit as December approaches.
explanation.definitionFit: Being convinced means being sure, persuaded, the adjective sense of certain.

clue.text: Lack of interest in vase around northern clubs formerly

indicators.note: around means encircling, so the first word wraps round what follows

parts.note: C is clubs, the card suit

explanation.surface: Apathy shown towards a vase once owned by northern clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: U(N + C + ONCE)RN.
explanation.definitionFit: Unconcern is indifference, an absence of caring or attention about something.

clue.text: Skull in opening of chiller set on an island possessed by spirit

indicators.note: in a down clue, set on means placed on top, so this piece comes first
the opening of a word is its first letter
something possessed by another is held inside it

parts.note: I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A skull found in a horror story, with ghosts haunting an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' suggests a ghost; it is the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The cranium is the part of the skull enclosing the brain, often used for the whole skull.

clue.text: Son in trouble with English passage

indicators.note: with means alongside, so the last piece is joined on
in places one piece inside the next

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A boy in difficulties with an English text passage.
explanation.walkthrough: AI(S)L + E.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is a walkway between rows of seats, a passage in a church or theatre.

clue.text: Woman before reform not having a refuge

indicators.note: in a down clue, before means the first piece comes above the next
not having something means it is taken out

parts.note: to alter is to change, reform

explanation.surface: A woman, before changing her ways, had nowhere to go.
explanation.walkthrough: SHE + ALTER without its A.
explanation.definitionFit: A shelter is a place of safety or protection, the same as a refuge.

clue.text: Items broadcast after hesitation in time before Christmas commercial

indicators.note: in places these pieces inside the following word

parts.note: Advent is the church season leading up to Christmas

indicators.note: after means the shuffled piece follows the other
broadcast means scattered widely, as seed is sown, so the letters are strewn

explanation.surface: TV items aired after a pause in the run-up to Christmas are commercials.
explanation.walkthrough: ADV(ER + TISEM)ENT. 'Broadcast' and 'commercial' fit TV, but broadcast is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A commercial is a TV or radio advertisement, so the noun senses match.

clue.text: Brief dispatch

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a task or area of responsibility given to someone
second meaning: to send off, especially money

explanation.walkthrough: Brief looks like an adjective meaning short; here it is the noun, a set of instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: A remit is the scope of one's assigned job, and to remit payment is to send it off.

clue.text: Street speaker's source of inspiration

indicators.note: a speaker's version is what the ear hears, not how it is written

explanation.surface: A street orator draws on some inspiration.
explanation.walkthrough: A mews is a British street of former stables, now usually converted to homes.
explanation.definitionFit: A mews is a narrow back lane of converted stables, used as a residential road name.

clue.text: Witticism in record, one with good force

indicators.note: with means alongside, so the pieces are joined in sequence

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A clever one-liner on a recording that hits home hard.
explanation.definitionFit: An epigram is a short, pointed and clever saying, a witty remark.

clue.text: Call film about tango mystifying

indicators.note: about means going round, so one word surrounds the letter

parts.note: pic is short for picture, a film
Tango is T in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Calling a dance film baffling.
explanation.walkthrough: CRY + PI(T)C.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic means obscure or puzzling in meaning, hence mystifying to the reader.

clue.text: Terrible tedium is broken by one with line creating likeness

indicators.note: broken by means split open with something pushed in the gap
something terrible is in a dreadful state, so these letters are wrecked and reordered
with means alongside, so the two inserted pieces are joined

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: Awful boredom is relieved by someone with a good line in imitation.
explanation.walkthrough: SIM(I + L)ITUDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Similitude is a resemblance or similarity, a formal word for a likeness.

clue.text: Not working on the house

definitions.meaning: second meaning: given at no charge

explanation.walkthrough: 'On the house' sounds like a roofer at work; it is the pub idiom for no charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Free means both at liberty with time on one's hands and costing nothing, which 'on the house' idiomatically means.
